You are grading an AI assistant's answer to a question about a company handbook.

Question: In the United States, how does GitLab differentiate between a regular vacation day and a parental leave request?
Reference answer (written from the handbook): GitLab calls a regular vacation day "time off" and a parental leave request "leave". The former is a short, everyday absence, while the latter is a longer, approved absence for a specific life circumstance.

Passages the assistant was given:
"""
[New Hires, Celebrations and Significant Life Events > New Hire Swag > Celebrations > Team Member Birthdays]
GitLab encourages team members to take a day of vacation on their special day in alignment with our **[Paid Time Off Policy](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/time-off-types/)**. If your celebration happens to fall over a weekend please be sure to take an alternate day such as the Friday prior or the Monday after.

[Leave of Absence > Company-Wide Leave of Absence Policies > Parental Leave]
GitLab's paid Parental Leave is for any team member (regardless of gender) who becomes a parent through child birth or adoption.  To learn more about our Parental Leave policy and eligibility requirements, please refer to the [Parental Leave](/handbook/people-group/time-off-and-absence/leave-types/#gitlab-parental-leave) section in our handbook.

[United States Leave of Absence Policies > How to Request Leave (Effective 2026-02-02) > U.S Military Leave]
GitLab, Inc. recognizes the obligation of those team members serving in any branch of the military or other uniformed services of the United States. Employment status within GitLab is protected by the Uniformed Services Employment and Reemployment Rights Act of 1994 ("USERRA").

**Leave and Re-Employment**

Team members who serve on active or reserve duty will be granted a leave of absence up to the maximum time required by law. GitLab is committed to preserving the job rights of team members absent on military leave in accordance with law.

**Compensation**

Team members on **unpaid** military leave will be paid at 100% of their salary for the first 31 calendar days of leave. Exempt team members will not incur any reduction in pay for partial week absences for leave under this policy.

Team members who **receive payment by the military or government** during their military leave will receive supplemental top-up pay equal to 100% of your total weekly wages for the first 31 calendar days of leave. 

**Health Care Continuation**

During a military leave of less than 31 days, a team member is entitled to continued group health plan coverage under the same conditions as if the employee had continued to work. For military leaves of more than 30 days, an employee may elect to continue their health coverage in accordance with USERRA and COBRA. For additional information on health care continuation contact the Absence Management team in Compass.

[United States Leave of Absence Policies > How to Request Leave (Effective 2026-02-02) > Which leave is right for me? > How Will My Pay Be Calculated?]
| Leave Program | Pay Calculations |
|:---:|:---:|
| Parental Leave | 100% paid by GitLab (minus any State Disability and/or Paid Family Leave benefits) |
| [Family Medical Leave Act(FMLA - Own Condition)](#payroll-processing-during-fmla) | 66.67% (STD) + 33.3% paid by GitLab per weekAfter 26 weeks:       66.67% (LTD) per month |
| [Family Medical Leave Act(FMLA - Care for a Family Member)](#the-family-medical-leave-act-fmla) | 100% for up to 25 working days |
| California Family Rights Act(CFRA) | First 8 weeks:  60% (SDI/PFL) + 6.66% (STD) + 33.3% paid by GitLab8-12 weeks:  60% (SDI - if applicable) + 6.66% (STD) + 33.3% paid by GitLabAfter 26 weeks:  66.67% LTD paid by Cigna monthly (if eligible) |
| [Military Leave (USERRA)](#us-military-leave) | Please see the Compensation heading under the [US Military Leave Policy](/handbook/people-policies/leave-of-absence/us/#us-military-leave) |

*If leave is taken continuously

If you live in a state where disability or paid family leave benefits are available, GitLab will offset your pay minus these benefits. Please refer to GitLab's [Parental Leave](/handbook/total-rewards/benefits/general-and-entity-benefits/#parental-leave) policy for more information.

[GitLab Korea Limited Benefits > We've Got You Covered > Time Off Policies > Statutory Vacation]
- Team members with 0-1 year of service are entitled to 1 day/month or 12 days/year.
- Team members with 1-3 years of service are entitled to 1.25 days/month or 15 days/year.
- Team members with 3+ years of service are entitled to one additional day for every two years continuously worked up to 25 days/year.
- Accrual balances reset January 1st of every year.

[United States Leave of Absence Policies > How to Request Leave (Effective 2026-02-02) > Which leave is right for me? > California Family Rights Act (CFRA)]
GitLab will grant time off to eligible team members in accordance with the requirements of the California Family Rights Act ("CFRA") and the federal Family and Medical Leave Act (Fed-FMLA). Where both the CFRA and Fed-FMLA apply, the leave provided by each will count against the team member's entitlement under both laws and must be taken concurrently. A team member who is eligible for leave under only one of these laws will receive benefits in accordance with that law only. In any case, team members will be eligible for the most generous benefits available under applicable law.

The following policy addresses team member rights under the CFRA only. Team members should refer to [GitLab's Team Member Handbook](#the-family-medical-leave-act-fmla) for additional detail regarding the Fed-FMLA. All questions concerning this policy should be directed to Tilt.

**Team Member Eligibility**

To be eligible for CFRA leave, team members who reside in California must have been employed by the Company for a total of at least 12 months (52 weeks) at any time prior to the commencement of the leave and have worked at least 1,250 hours over the previous 12 months as of the start of the leave.

**Qualifying Reasons For Leave**

Eligible team members may request leave under the CFRA for one or more of the following reasons:

- correctness: "correct" if the answer states the key information in the reference answer without contradicting it (extra correct detail is fine); "partial" if it gets part of it or is vague; "incorrect" if it is wrong, contradicts the reference, or does not answer.
